newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO PESO ENDS SOFT ON DOLLAR SHORT-COVERING.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO PESO ENDS SOFT ON DOLLAR SHORT-COVERING.

text.p: The Mexican peso retained its midday losses at the close on Thursday.
Dealers said the peso reversed its early strength on dollar short-covering and some speculation.
"Dollars were on offer at the open, but banks stepped in to cover shorts mid-morning and that weaknened the peso," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 2.95 and 2.7 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.8075/7.8125 and 7.8030/7.8080 per dollar.

Dealers said speculation partly drove demand for dollars because market forecasts that mild inflation data and positive trade surplus figures were about to be published would normally have tended to bolster the peso.
Some traders said the peso had also weakened due to foreign investors taking profits on the local bourse and switching to dollars.
Same-day peso contracts had closed trade mid-morning 0.8 of a centavo weaker at 7.7770/7.7820 per dollar.
